title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous one. There Grothendieck wrote 𝓔_X^{X̃} for the profinite étale fundamental group of a connected ('0-connexe') scheme X, based not at a point but at a universal cover X̃, or more generally at any simply connected ('1-connexe') X-scheme T used as a fibre functor. He also noted that (X, X̃) ↦ 𝓔_X^{X̃} is a functor.

On this page:
(8) For a morphism of geometrically pointed schemes f:(X,ξ)→(Y,η) one gets π_1(X,ξ)→π_1(Y,η).
- A geometric point of X at x is a separably closed extension Ω of k(x).
- Through k(y)↪k(x), Ω is also an extension of k(y). So the point canonically induces a geometric point of Y at y=f(x).
(9) The map (8) can therefore be rewritten as π_1(X, k(x)^sep) → π_1(Y, k(y)^sep), using the separable closures inside Ω. This works because fibre functors of finite étale covers only see the separable closure.
(10) He defines the relative fundamental group 𝓔_{X/Y}^{X̃} := Ker(π_1(X,X̃) → π_1(Y,X̃)). Here π_1(Y,X̃) is identified with π_1(Y,Ỹ), where Ỹ is the universal cover of Y determined by the composite X̃→Y.

The next page:
- generalises this to any triple T→X→Y with T simply connected;
- lists special cases: the geometric fundamental group π_1(X/A), and π_1 of B/A for rings;
- states the real goal, a 'universal homotopy exact sequence' in dimension 2 attached to X→Y.

Purpose: in the Longue Marche context, π_1(X/k) = Ker(π_1(X)→Gal(k̄/k)) is the geometric fundamental group π_1(X_{k̄}). The extension 1→π_1(X/k)→π_1(X)→Gal→1 is the basic object of anabelian geometry and of the Galois action on Teichmüller groupoids. This page sets up its functorial, base-point-flexible formalism.
errors: No mathematical error. The transcribed 'd'où un homomorphisme de schémas' inverts the logic. The morphism of geometrically pointed schemes is the hypothesis and (8) the consequence, so the reading should be 'si on a un homomorphisme' / 'pour un homomorphisme'.

Minor point left implicit: the identification π_1(Y,X̃)=π_1(Y,Ỹ) needs Ỹ to be the universal cover through which X̃→Y factors. This holds, since X̃ is simply connected, so the map factors through a universal cover of Y, unique up to unique isomorphism given the fibre point.

ideas.what: Functoriality of the étale π_1 for morphisms of geometrically pointed schemes. The geometric point of the target is induced by composing residue field extensions, and only separable closures matter.
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of the étale fundamental group

ideas.what: Using a universal cover, or any simply connected T over X, as the 'base point' (fibre functor) for π_1.
ideas.modern_name: fibre functors / pro-representable base points (universal pro-covering as base point)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1; later Deligne (tangential base points, 1989)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (pro-representability of fibre functors); spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group π_1(X/Y) defined as Ker(π_1(X)→π_1(Y)), functorial in triples T→X→Y.
ideas.modern_name: relative / geometric fundamental group; kernel in the fundamental exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1 Exp. IX-X (homotopy exact sequence); standard in anabelian geometry

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping on functoriality and base points of π_1, plus the definition of a kernel. Everything here is standard from SGA1. The more interesting 'universal homotopy exact sequence in dimension 2' is only announced on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'd'où [?] un homomorphisme de schémas "géométriquement pointés"' should read approximately 'si on a un homom. de schémas "géométriquement pointés"'.
'ext. sép. clos[?]' should read 'ext. sép. close'.
In (8) the target subscript is Y (written, possibly corrected) with superscript η. The transcription's crossing-out marks do not change the meaning.
'— d'où[?] l'homomorphisme (8)' is more likely '— et l'homomorphisme (8) s'identifie aussi à'.
The number in the lower left margin is 107, the archive page number.
